said: the bars to the left are right, why are there there still... please fix these bars, for the love of god... The bars are still there
what: Vertical bars flank the picture at any window that is not 16:9. Scale.FIT maps a fixed 1920x1080 design into a differently-shaped window; the remainder is a gap. Five fixes all answered 'what colour should the gap be' rather than removing it.
rootCause: Width was over-constrained. FR-8's fall time needs a fixed fall DISTANCE, which is vertical, so height must stay 1080 — but the width was pinned at 1920 alongside it for no independent reason.
evidence: FIXED AT THE SOURCE. GAME_WIDTH is now a live binding set at boot from the window's aspect at a pinned 1080 height (FR-8 needs a fixed fall DISTANCE, which is vertical). Three frozen module-level captures were found and fixed. Verified by decoding the PNGs: at 2560x1080 columns x=0 and x=2559 carry identical values to x=60 and x=2499; at the user's 2000x1010 exactly one column differs by ~0.2px of rounding, painted sky, against the 102px slab at rgb(16,41,80) it replaced. NOTE: the world widens but never narrows (MIN_ASPECT 16/9) because narrowing CROPS content — Beacon Log ran 384px off the right edge at 1440. Windows narrower than 16:9 therefore keep TOP and BOTTOM bars; the side bars are gone at every ratio.

said: is there a reason why the world is made up of a bunch of vertical strips, it looks like about 8 and the just looked stitched together, and sliding from left to right, why was it built this way?
what: Visible vertical seams across the sky; the world reads as stitched panels drifting sideways.
rootCause: Measured 41 vertical luminance steps (0.35-2.4) across the upper sky at irregular spacing. Two contributors: wrapXY duplicates sub-planes in BOTH axes for 'sideways-drifting' layers, in a game that scrolls VERTICALLY; and shapes clipped at tile edges leave hard boundaries.
evidence: atmospherePass called the RNG inside the wrap loop, so the three 'wrapped' copies of each streak had different y values — they were never copies. Every 256px carried a hard discontinuity: 7.5 joins at 1920 wide, and the user counted 'about 8'. Endpoints are now computed once, copies are pure translations wrapped in both axes, texture 256->512, and the sideways drift is gone — a weather pass sliding horizontally in a vertically-scrolling world was motion in an axis nothing else moves in.

said: theres a pop every so often in the game like its being looped. Should be continous.
what: An audible pop/click recurs during play. NOT a loop seam: it is a step change in the music layer gains whenever an intensity crossfade is interrupted by another one.
rootCause: MusicBus.setIndex restarted the crossfade from the abandoned TARGET INDEX rather than from the gains the layers were actually holding, so the next frame wrote layerTargetGains(oldTarget) and every in-flight layer snapped to its destination in one frame. setFromState runs every frame off the live asteroid count, so the index recrosses a threshold inside the 1400 ms ramp constantly during play - which is the 'every so often'. The C12 ambient-bed loop seam was the prime suspect and was DISPROVEN by measurement; it was fixed anyway as a separate real defect.
evidence: Two renders of the real MusicBus layer trajectory, differenced (identical oscillators, so the difference IS the artifact): 1.49e-8 in the 2 ms before the interrupt, 0.0154 one sample later, peaking at 0.0184 = 23% of the music bus RMS (0.0799). Zero to a quarter of the mix in one sample. The gain step at the interrupt frame was 0.04099 against the ramp's own largest per-frame move of 0.00299 - 13.7x - and 0.155 (52x) with the belt thrashing across both thresholds. After the fix: gain step 0.0000198 (0.01x), rendered artifact 2.7% of RMS, and the interrupted trajectory's max per-frame move equals the smooth ramp's exactly. Tests watched fail first: tests/unit/audio/music.test.ts 'UR-10: an intensity change never steps a layer gain' - 3 tests, bar is the ramp's OWN measured max per-frame move, not a constant. C12 ELIMINATED: the wind loop seam is real (0.2873 jump vs 0.0844 largest interior step, every 4.000 s) and is fixed by folding the walk's tail over its head, but it is NOT audible - recording the live game's master through an AudioWorklet and phase-averaging the high-passed envelope at the 4 s lap with the wrap off then on gave 5.0x and 6.1x the phase median, indistinguishable. No pre-rendered bed is needed for this ticket. AmbientBus has the identical defect (54.7x gain step on an interrupted bed crossfade) but fixing it overturns a tested behaviour; escalated in gauntlet/escalations.md.

said: How are we doing on music as well, did we get that settled? ... I mean actual music for the game, I didnt here any melodys, did we write music for the game?
what: There is no music. No melody, no rhythm, no theme anywhere in the game.
rootCause: music.ts implements AC-21.2's STRUCTURE correctly — three cumulative intensity layers, index a pure function of live game state, equal-power crossfades — but the content is an oscillator stack. Each layer is a sustained CHORD (partialsHz: 'A chord, not a note, so a layer has body'). D63 called for 'composed files with intensity layers'; the file records why it is not: 'No key and no composer exists yet, so the layers are synthesised here.' That reason is now stale — there is a key — but the ElevenLabs Music API returns 402 on the free tier.
evidence: Verified: /v1/music and /v1/music/compose both return 402 paid_plan_required. /v1/sound-generation DOES work on the free tier and supports loop:true, which is the fix for UR-10's seam. The swap point is already built and named in music.ts: 'Replacing the oscillator stack in buildLayerVoice with three looping AudioBufferSourceNodes is the whole change.'
